obligations.statement: The facade produces the canonical, deterministic rendering selected by the work item's acceptance field and resolves citations according to the stated grammar.
obligations.source: LIFE-D1: "The field selects; the renderer resolves," including the rendering, resolution, generated-ID, refusal, repository-root, and grammar-compatibility rules.

parts.statement: The acceptance field's resolved selection is canonical, with no separate editable review copy, and cited spec edits flow through without copying text.
Citations resolve to complete entries in field order under the stated citation syntax, independently of working directory and for pre-existing items.
Text and mixed fields receive stable, unique IDs in the consumer grammar, while explicit IDs survive unchanged.
Each generated ID is derived from the item ID and the source line's nonblank position.
Invalid references, spec failures, duplicate IDs, and collisions are refused with the offending ID or path and cause.
The description is separately headed and cannot be parsed as criteria by existing consumers.
Only the description, acceptance field, and named spec affect rendered bytes.
Empty cited entries contribute no criterion.
The workcli and spec-lint grammars remain explicitly marked counterparts.
Both grammars parse the shared round-trip fixture to the same entries.

obligations.statement: Each item is classified into the correct attack-document lifecycle, with canonical storage and reusable closed evidence.
obligations.source: LIFE-D2: "One document is attacked for each item," including spec-born and tracker-born classification, storage paths, workflow, reuse, and generated-directory rules.

parts.statement: Citation-only items attack the whole named spec, while any full-text line makes the item tracker-born and attacks its rendering.
The quality review of a spec-born item judges its criterion selection, work-item coverage, and slice assignment.
An empty spec-born selection remains unclaimable.
The tracker-born workflow renders to the canonical path, attacks, checks, commits both files, attests, and reuses unchanged valid evidence.
The generated attack directory exists in fresh checkouts and is exempt from authored-prose doc-lint.
A manually edited tracker-born snapshot cannot replace a fresh rendering or count as an amendment.

obligations.statement: Attestation binds an item to one closed attack record for the current attacked bytes and fails safely for invalid evidence.
obligations.source: LIFE-D3: "Attestation binds to the attacked content," including marker contents, refusal conditions, idempotency, fresh rendering, and malformed-marker behavior.

parts.statement: The marker contains a parseable timestamp.
The marker binds the attacked byte digest, excludes paths from that digest, and permits a coordinated content-preserving rename.
Every stated binding or closure violation is refused without writing a marker.
Repeated or concurrent requests for the same valid attestation leave one marker.
The attack path attests only after the checker succeeds.
Consumers ignore malformed markers and name unreadable marker sources.

obligations.statement: Amendments invalidate old evidence before reuse and require renewed attack and attestation for the changed contract.
obligations.source: LIFE-D4: "Amendments invalidate evidence before reuse," including byte-change rules, the amendment trail, full re-attack, concurrency, and briefing instructions.

parts.statement: Tracker-born rendering changes, spec byte changes, and spec-born description-only changes have the stated invalidation effects.
A field amendment uses the existing `work acceptance set --why` trail.
Any attacked-document byte change requires a full new round and renewed attestation before use.
Dispatch briefs and post-halt instructions cite the quality standard and before-use re-attack rule.
A later concurrent amendment is detected by the next consuming boundary.

obligations.statement: Claim, delivery, review, and posting enforce the noun, criteria, triviality, attestation, role, and diagnostic rules in LIFE-D5.
obligations.source: LIFE-D5: the transition table and the paragraphs governing open versus in-progress claims, existing items, diagnostics, semantic neutrality, structural roles, placeholders, and unknown types.

parts.statement: An open noun-bearing leaf with empty or unresolvable criteria is refused, while an already-in-progress claim is a no-op.
Every open-to-in-progress verb applies the exact noun and triviality attestation rules.
PR delivery enforces resolvable criteria and current attestation under the stated triviality rule.
Installing the facade does not rewrite existing work items.
Review emission and verdict posting apply their LIFE-D5 rows.
No gate classifies or refuses otherwise valid criteria because of their wording.
Design children bypass claim and delivery gates, implementation placeholders remain unclaimable, and unknown item types are refused.
Claim and delivery refusals name the prescribed remedy or failing reference.
A design child's present spec record remains subject to the repository record gate.

obligations.statement: Review emission and verdict posting use the exact current rendered contract and never validate a stale verdict through re-attestation alone.
obligations.source: LIFE-D6: "Review and posting use the rendered contract," including freshness, recorded bytes, section extraction, failure behavior, and the no-item path.

parts.statement: Item-linked review input equals a fresh rendering and is recorded with the emitted round.
Posting requires equality with both the judged bytes and a fresh rendering, including after re-attacked amendments.
Both consumers refuse empty criteria, missing required attestation, and rendering failure without falling back to an unchecked file.
The poster extracts criteria only from the acceptance-criteria section.
A review target with no work item retains the existing supplied-file path.

obligations.statement: The whole-repository CI gate checks every tracked attack record, fails safely when checking is unavailable, and respects its defined inventory boundary.
obligations.source: LIFE-D7 and its what-if row: tracked-record enumeration, invalid categories, missing dependencies, inventory exclusions, repeated-check behavior, and required-lens migration.

parts.statement: One run reports every invalid tracked record and cause, including paths for a missing attacked document.
Missing checker or failed tracked-record enumeration prevents success.
Ignored, untracked, and other-checkout records are excluded, and an empty inventory passes.
Repeated checks of the same tree have equal results and write nothing.
Existing committed records are migrated before a newly required lens is enforced on the default branch.

obligations.statement: Consumers adopt new facade verbs through safe version checks, and unsupported tools hand Claude-only rounds through the existing workflow.
obligations.source: LIFE-D8 and its what-if row: installed-version checks, semantic-version precedence, delivery completion, user-controlled installation, Claude-only rounds, handoff, and non-mutating reads.

parts.statement: A consumer refuses an insufficient or unestablished facade version by name and calls the new verb only after a sufficient semantic version is established.
Facade delivery is incomplete until the installed command reports the shipping version.
Non-Claude tools hand attack and review rounds to a Claude Code session through the existing delivery workflow.
Version checks are read-only and do not change item state.
Briefs cite the shared quality standard and the before-use amendment rule.

obligations.statement: Lifecycle testing is isolated from deployed configuration and the user's real tracker.
obligations.source: Testing decisions: "Use the workcli fake backend" and "No test deploys configuration or rewrites the user's tracker."

parts.statement: No lifecycle test deploys configuration or rewrites the user's tracker.

obligations.statement: Component child specs fix their contracts before implementation and preserve the parent contract.
obligations.source: Testing decisions: "Component child specs define wire formats and fixtures before scaffolding. They retain these public contracts and may not weaken parent invariants or leave significant product decisions to implementation."

parts.statement: Component child specs define wire formats and fixtures before scaffolding.
Component child specs preserve parent public contracts and invariants and close significant product decisions before implementation.

obligations.statement: The ordered slice and continuation workflow preserves dependency order, tracker topology, cross-slice verification, and open parent evidence.
obligations.source: Ordered slice list and Continuations: the explicit after-S2/after-S3 dependencies, `work promote`, design child, blocked placeholder, manifests, verification children, and parent-evidence rule.

parts.statement: Slices are specified, implemented, and enabled in the stated dependency order.
Each feature is promoted before implementation and has the required design child and blocked implementation placeholder.
Each child spec supplies its implementation manifest and dependencies and names a verification child for parent outcomes spanning slices.
Delivering a design child does not discharge parent criteria or change their open evidence rows.

obligations.statement: Lifecycle bookkeeping does not substitute for implementation evidence or pending human acceptance.
obligations.source: Evidence: "A valid ledger, closed attack record, or passing lifecycle gate does not establish implementation success or discharge a pending human acceptance check."

parts.statement: A ledger, attack record, or lifecycle gate alone cannot establish implementation success or discharge pending human acceptance.

ground.reason: LIFE-D1 calls parser compatibility across repositories an obligation, but LIFE-A28 checks agreement only on one shared fixture. Both parsers can mishandle the same unrepresented grammar case while passing that check.

objections.objection: The criterion lets fixture agreement stand in for compatibility across the supported grammar.
objections.obligation: The workcli renderer and spec-lint remain compatible for valid criterion entries.

scenario.given: Both parsers produce identical entries for the shared fixture but interpret an unrepresented continuation or criterion-shaped line differently.
scenario.when: LIFE-A28's shared-fixture comparison runs.
scenario.expect: The fixture comparison passes while the parsers disagree on another valid entry shape, so cross-repository compatibility is absent.

ground.reason: LIFE-D4 says amended criteria must be attacked again before use. LIFE-A32 checks only that two instruction artifacts cite that rule and the quality standard. Text can contain those citations without the workflow enforcing them.

objections.objection: The criterion lets instructional text substitute for the promised prevention of using amended criteria before another attack.
objections.obligation: Dispatch and post-halt workflows do not use amended criteria until those criteria have been attacked again.

scenario.given: The dispatch brief and review-halt instructions contain the required citations, but their workflow continues after an amendment without checking for a new closed attack.
scenario.when: LIFE-A32 is checked by inspecting the two instruction artifacts.
scenario.expect: The citation check passes while the amended criteria are used without another attack.

ground.reason: LIFE-A22 combines independently deliverable first-run orchestration, commit ordering, attestation readiness, and unchanged-state reuse. The initial workflow can work while reuse still launches another attack round.

objections.objection: The criterion has no separate acceptance result for the reuse behavior, so successful first-run orchestration can conceal an independently failing idempotency obligation.
objections.obligation: An unchanged second invocation reuses current files and evidence without starting another attack round.

scenario.given: The workflow renders, attacks, commits, and attests correctly on its first invocation, but always starts a new model round on a second unchanged invocation.
scenario.when: The criterion is evaluated through the successful first-run workflow.
scenario.expect: The first-run workflow check passes while the promised unchanged-state reuse is absent.

ground.reason: The Testing decisions section names broad techniques, while component specs are deferred to define wire formats and fixtures. The Evidence section leaves every criterion open. No criterion-level contract fixes required setups, evidence, acceptance authority, or the completion that waits on the result.

objections.objection: The set permits implementer-selected checks to be treated as acceptance evidence even when they do not distinguish a promised behavior from a plausible partial implementation.
objections.obligation: Each LIFE-A criterion has a binding public-interface check with specified setup, observation, pass/fail rule, evidence, authority, and dependent completion.

scenario.given: An implementation passes chosen happy-path fixtures but fails a required boundary such as legacy-item rendering or a concurrent attestation request.
scenario.when: Acceptance is attempted using only the document's generic testing guidance.
scenario.expect: The selected checks pass and the work can be presented for acceptance while an untested promised case remains absent.

ground.reason: LIFE-A2 checks stability, uniqueness, grammar, and preservation of explicit IDs, but it does not require generated IDs to derive from both the item ID and the text line's nonblank position. The source passage says: "text without an ID receives a deterministic positional ID derived from the item ID and its nonblank position."

objections.objection: The renderer may generate stable unique IDs from the text alone and still pass every criterion, despite violating the required positional derivation.

scenario.given: An implementation passes LIFE-A1 through LIFE-A33 and generates stable unique IDs by hashing criterion text.
scenario.when: Two items render identical unlabelled criterion text at different positions.
scenario.expect: The generated ID is unrelated to the item ID or nonblank position.

ground.reason: LIFE-A28 checks the shared fixture's parsed result, but no criterion observes whether the workcli and spec-lint grammars remain explicitly marked as counterparts. The source passage says: "The workcli and spec-lint grammars remain marked counterparts with a common round-trip fixture."

objections.objection: The counterpart markers may be removed while the current shared fixture continues to pass.

scenario.given: Both parsers produce the same entries for the current round-trip fixture and all criteria pass.
scenario.when: The counterpart annotations are deleted.
scenario.expect: Neither grammar identifies the other as its compatibility counterpart.

ground.reason: LIFE-A23 checks that assigned IDs are stored as citations, and LIFE-A29 checks that a spec-born item attacks the whole spec. Neither checks that the quality review judges the item's selection and slice assignment. The source passage says: "Selection and work-item coverage are judged by the quality review of the spec and its slice assignments."

objections.objection: A spec-born item may cite a valid but incomplete or wrongly assigned criterion set without any lifecycle criterion requiring that assignment to be judged.

scenario.given: The whole spec has a closed attack record, the item stores valid citations, and all lifecycle criteria pass.
scenario.when: The item's cited selection is not examined for coverage of its assigned slice.
scenario.expect: The item reaches gated use even though its slice assignment omits an outcome allocated to that item.

ground.reason: LIFE-A6 observes one content-revision attestation, but no criterion requires the marker to contain a parseable timestamp. The source passage says: "The marker contains a parseable timestamp and the digest of the attacked document's bytes."

objections.objection: An attestation marker with no timestamp, or with an unparsable timestamp, may satisfy every criterion.

scenario.given: The marker is unique, current, and accepted by all checks.
scenario.when: A valid closed record is attested.
scenario.expect: The marker binds the correct digest but has no parseable timestamp.

ground.reason: The amendment criteria cover invalidation and renewed attack, but none observes the required audit trail. The source passage says: "An amendment uses the existing `work acceptance set --why` trail where the field changes."

objections.objection: Acceptance text may be amended through an untracked write that invalidates and renews evidence correctly but records no reason.

scenario.given: The amendment is rerendered, attacked, committed, re-attested, and passes every criterion.
scenario.when: The acceptance field is changed without using `work acceptance set --why`.
scenario.expect: The amended field has no `--why` trail.

ground.reason: LIFE-A1 checks that pre-existing items render correctly, but no criterion observes installation for unintended tracker writes. The source passage says: "Installing the facade does not rewrite existing items."

objections.objection: Installation may rewrite existing items while preserving values well enough for all later rendering and gate checks to pass.

scenario.given: Their effective descriptions and acceptance fields remain unchanged, so every behavioral criterion passes.
scenario.when: The facade is installed over a repository containing existing items.
scenario.expect: Existing tracker records are rewritten during installation.

ground.reason: LIFE-A16 concerns review emission for an item, and LIFE-A17 checks item-linked posting. Neither preserves the non-item workflow. The source passage says: "A target with no work item keeps the existing supplied-file path."

objections.objection: The supplied-file review path may be removed without failing any item-linked review or posting criterion.

scenario.given: All item-linked emission and posting checks pass.
scenario.when: A caller emits a review round without naming a work item.
scenario.expect: A review target with no work item cannot use the existing supplied criteria file.

ground.reason: LIFE-A18 through LIFE-A20 constrain which records are reported and how dependency failures behave, but they do not require repeated checks to be deterministic or non-mutating. The what-if passage says: "Repeated checks over the same tree have equal results; checks write nothing."

objections.objection: The CI check may alter records or return different results on an unchanged checkout while still satisfying its inventory and reporting criteria on the tested invocation.

scenario.given: Each individual invocation reports the required invalid records and causes.
scenario.when: The gate is run twice against the same tracked checkout.
scenario.expect: The first CI invocation writes state, causing a different result on the second unchanged invocation.

ground.reason: LIFE-A18 requires invalid records to be reported, but no criterion requires the migration ordering promised for a newly required lens. The source passage says: "A change adding a lens must update existing committed records before the new requirement is enforced on the default branch."

objections.objection: A new required lens may be enforced before existing records are migrated, making the default branch red while every steady-state CI criterion remains satisfiable.

scenario.given: The checker correctly uses the new registry and reports all now-invalid records.
scenario.when: The required-lens registry is changed before existing records are updated.
scenario.expect: Existing committed records become invalid on the default branch before their migration lands.

ground.reason: LIFE-A21 checks consumer behavior for sufficient and insufficient versions, but no criterion makes the installed command's reported version a completion condition for facade delivery. The source passage says: "Facade delivery is complete only when the installed command reports that version."

objections.objection: Facade delivery may be declared complete while the installed command still reports an older version.

scenario.given: Unit and integration checks for LIFE-A21 pass using controlled version responses.
scenario.when: The new facade build is delivered without the user installing it.
scenario.expect: Delivery is recorded as complete although the installed facade lacks the shipping version.

ground.reason: No criterion checks the required cross-tool handoff. The source passage says: "Other tools hand those rounds to a Claude Code session through the existing delivery workflow."

objections.objection: A non-Claude tool may fail locally or skip the attack or review instead of handing the round to Claude Code.

scenario.given: The Claude-only attack and review implementations and all listed criteria pass.
scenario.when: A supported non-Claude tool reaches an attack or review round.
scenario.expect: No Claude Code handoff occurs and the required round is not run.

ground.reason: LIFE-A21 determines whether a verb is called after a version check, but it does not require the version check itself to preserve item state. The what-if passage says: "Version checks are reads and change no item state."

objections.objection: Reading the installed version may mutate the work item before the consumer makes its version decision.

scenario.given: The returned version and subsequent refuse-or-call behavior satisfy LIFE-A21.
scenario.when: A consumer performs its prerequisite version check.
scenario.expect: The item's notes or metadata change as a side effect of obtaining the version.

ground.reason: No criterion observes the test-safety guarantee. The source passage says: "No test deploys configuration or rewrites the user's tracker."

objections.objection: The test suite may pass while deploying configuration or modifying the user's real tracker.

scenario.given: All functional assertions required by LIFE-A1 through LIFE-A33 pass.
scenario.when: The lifecycle test suite is executed in a user's checkout.
scenario.expect: A passing test run changes deployed configuration or real tracker state.

ground.reason: No criterion observes whether component child specs define their wire formats and fixtures before scaffolding. The source passage says: "Component child specs define wire formats and fixtures before scaffolding."

objections.objection: Implementation may be scaffolded before the component contracts and fixtures are fixed.

scenario.given: The completed implementation later passes every parent acceptance criterion.
scenario.when: A component slice begins implementation.
scenario.expect: The implementation exists before its child spec defines the wire format and fixtures.

ground.reason: Passing the parent behavior does not inspect the content or decision closure of component child specs. The source passage says: "They retain these public contracts and may not weaken parent invariants or leave significant product decisions to implementation."

objections.objection: A child spec may weaken a parent invariant or delegate a significant product decision to implementation even if the resulting implementation happens to pass the parent criteria.

scenario.given: The chosen implementation passes all LIFE criteria.
scenario.when: The component child spec is reviewed as a deliverable.
scenario.expect: The child spec contains a weaker contract or leaves a significant observable choice unresolved.

ground.reason: The ordered slice section imposes sequencing dependencies, but no criterion observes the order in which slices are specified, implemented, or enabled. The relevant passages include: "after S2," "after the attack path is available," and "after S3."

objections.objection: Slices may be implemented or enabled out of the required order while the final combined behavior passes every criterion.

scenario.given: All slices eventually produce behavior satisfying LIFE-A1 through LIFE-A33.
scenario.when: S4 or S6 is enabled before the S3 attack path is available.
scenario.expect: A dependent slice is enabled before its required predecessor.

ground.reason: No criterion observes the required promotion and work-item topology. The source passage says: "Use `work promote` on each resulting feature before implementation. Its spec container holds a design child and blocked implementation placeholder."

objections.objection: Implementation may begin without promotion, a design child, or a blocked implementation placeholder.

scenario.given: The eventual implementation passes every lifecycle criterion.
scenario.when: A resulting feature proceeds directly to implementation.
scenario.expect: The feature lacks the required promoted container structure when implementation starts.

ground.reason: No criterion checks the required child-spec manifest, dependency declarations, or verification child. The source passage says: "The child spec supplies the implementation manifest and dependencies above. It names a verification child for any parent outcome spanning slices."

objections.objection: A child spec may omit its implementation manifest, dependencies, or cross-slice verification child.

scenario.given: Each implementation slice individually passes its allocated LIFE criteria.
scenario.when: The child spec and tracker structure are finalized.
scenario.expect: The tracker contains no verification child for a parent outcome that spans slices.

ground.reason: No criterion preserves the evidence state when design work is delivered. The source passage says: "Delivering the design does not discharge parent criteria or change their open evidence rows."

objections.objection: Delivering a design child may close parent criteria or alter their evidence rows before implementation evidence exists.

scenario.given: The design child is complete and all lifecycle behavior criteria remain independently satisfiable.
scenario.when: The design child is delivered.
scenario.expect: Parent criteria are marked discharged or their evidence rows cease to be open.

ground.reason: No criterion enforces the evidence limitation stated by the document. The source passage says: "A valid ledger, closed attack record, or passing lifecycle gate does not establish implementation success or discharge a pending human acceptance check."

objections.objection: The workflow may treat lifecycle bookkeeping as implementation evidence and close a pending human acceptance check.

scenario.given: The ledger is valid, the attack record is closed, and the lifecycle gate passes.
scenario.when: Completion is evaluated using those artifacts alone.
scenario.expect: A pending human acceptance check is marked discharged without being performed.

ground.reason: LIFE-A19 refuses to report success when the checker is unavailable, while LIFE-A20 succeeds whenever the tracked-record inventory is empty; both conditions can hold at once, and the criteria then demand opposite verdicts. LIFE-D7 carries the same tension ('Missing checker or failed enumeration is an error' alongside 'An empty inventory passes') without resolving which wins.

objections.objection: The criteria admit both a red and a green CI gate for the same tree: a checkout with no tracked attack records and a missing checker satisfies LIFE-A20's success condition and LIFE-A19's refusal condition simultaneously, so an implementer can pass or fail the gate by choosing which criterion to read.

scenario.given: A tracked checkout containing zero attack records under .work/attacks/ (enumeration over tracked files succeeds and returns an empty inventory), with the source-tree attack checker binary absent or non-executable.
scenario.when: The CI gate runs its whole-repo record check.
scenario.expect: LIFE-A19 requires the gate to refuse success (checker unavailable); LIFE-A20 requires the gate to succeed (inventory empty). The two verdicts conflict and no criterion states the precedence.

ground.reason: The attack-workflow criteria cover only the success path. The what-if table lists 'Attack or checker fails before attestation' as the dependency-failure answer for LIFE-A22, but no criterion states the resulting state: whether the rendering or record is committed, whether an attestation exists, and what the next invocation or gate observes.

objections.objection: A failed or interrupted tracker-born attack can leave an unspecified partial state — a rendered file or record committed without attestation, or vice versa — and no criterion pins what the system must look like afterward or what the next attack invocation must do with the leftover files.

scenario.given: a tracker-born item with valid criteria and no committed attack artifacts
scenario.when: the attack workflow renders the item and the checker then fails (or the process is interrupted after one file is committed)
scenario.expect: a defined end state — no attestation written, a named disposition for the partially written rendering and record, and a re-invocation that recovers deterministically — which no criterion checks

ground.reason: Nothing-changed repetition is unasked for verdict posting. LIFE-A17 pins only refusal conditions; the what-if row for LIFE-A16/A17 answers amendment-between-judgment-and-posting but never the case of posting the same verdict twice with nothing changed.

objections.objection: The criteria leave double-posting of a verdict unspecified: a second identical post with unchanged criteria and current attestation meets every LIFE-A17 precondition, so both 'accepted silently' and 'refused as duplicate' conform.

scenario.given: a verdict whose criteria match the round's recorded input and a fresh rendering, with current attestation, already posted once
scenario.when: the poster is invoked again with the identical verdict and unchanged item state
scenario.expect: a defined outcome — idempotent no-op, second post recorded, or named refusal — which no criterion checks

ground.reason: The repetition answer for the CI gate ('repeated checks over the same tree have equal results; checks write nothing') appears only in the what-if table. No acceptance criterion states that the gate is read-only or deterministic over an unchanged tree, so an implementation that writes or whose verdict flips between identical runs violates nothing testable.

objections.objection: The CI gate's claimed read-only, deterministic behavior is asserted in the document but untestable: LIFE-A18 to LIFE-A20 specify reporting for single runs and never bind two runs over the same tree to the same result or forbid writes.

scenario.given: a checkout whose tracked attack records are fixed
scenario.when: the CI gate runs twice in succession with no intervening change
scenario.expect: identical reports and no modification to the checkout, which no criterion checks

ground.reason: The nothing-changed question for a newly created spec-born item is unanswered. LIFE-A9 covers spec changes and LIFE-A6 covers attesting generically, but no criterion establishes that an item created after its spec's attack closed can attest against that existing record without a new attack round — LIFE-D2 says only that an empty selection stays unclaimable even when the spec was attacked.

objections.objection: It is unspecified whether a spec-born item minted after its spec's record closed may attest directly against that record or must trigger a fresh attack, so both a cheap attestation path and a mandatory new round conform to the criteria.

scenario.given: a spec whose attack record is closed at its current revision, and a new spec-born work item citing that spec's criteria
scenario.when: the item reaches a transition requiring attestation
scenario.expect: a defined path — attestation against the existing closed record, or a required new attack — which no criterion checks

dispositions.rationale: The gates enforce use before re-attack: LIFE-A8, A9, A14, A16 and A17 refuse stale or unattested criteria. LIFE-A32 pins only what the instruction text must say.

By LIFE-D1 and the testing decisions, component child specs fix each check's setup, fixtures and wire format before scaffolding. The parent names each check's public interface, and its evidence rows name the completion that waits.
Round 1 rejected this ground. LIFE-A2 holds the observable constraints: stable, unique and grammar-valid IDs. The derivation inputs are the spelling LIFE-D1 leaves to the component spec.
The counterpart markers are a maintenance device. LIFE-A28 observes the compatibility they protect.
Round 1 rejected this ground. The attack on the whole spec judges its slice assignments, and LIFE-A9 ties each spec-born attestation to that attack.
Round 1 rejected this ground. Nothing in this spec reads the marker's timestamp, and LIFE-D3 leaves the marker encoding to the facade component spec.
Round 1 rejected this ground. The --why trail is existing `work acceptance set` behaviour, and nothing in this spec changes it.
Round 1 rejected this ground. No slice includes a migration, so no implementation step could rewrite existing items.
Round 1 rejected this ground. This is the procedure for a future lens change, and no slice here builds it.
Installation is the user's action. The facade delivery item carries this as its own completion condition; it is not behaviour of any component this spec builds.
Round 1 rejected this ground. Claude-only rounds and their handoff are existing behaviour, unchanged here.
Round 1 rejected this ground. The testing decisions govern how the implementation is tested, and PR review judges them.
Round 1 rejected this ground. The lifecycle's own gates and each child spec's attack round enforce these on the child specs.
Round 1 rejected this ground. The lifecycle's own gates and each child spec's attack round enforce these on the child specs.
Slice order is enforced by tracker dependencies, not by an acceptance criterion.
Continuation structure is planning, not product behaviour, and the claim gates in LIFE-D5 enforce it on each promoted feature.
Round 1 rejected this ground. The lifecycle's own gates and each child spec's attack round enforce these on the child specs.
Evidence rows live in the spec document, which no delivery verb edits, so delivering a design child cannot change them.
This is a reading rule for evidence. No slice builds a consumer that could discharge a human check from lifecycle bookkeeping.

Verdict posting mechanics, including a repeated post, are existing poster behaviour. This spec adds only the criteria-freshness refusal, and a second post of unchanged criteria passes it as the first did.
LIFE-A6 covers it: attestation requires a valid closed record for the item's current document, whenever the item was created. LIFE-D2 reuses an unchanged record without a new round.
